subject: Urgent: Zenith Retail — sustained latency & error spikes / next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@zenithretail.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Urgent: production instability during flash sale

Alex —

We saw a multi-hour degradation yesterday during our Black Friday prep load test window (Nov 27, 18:30–21:10 ET). Symptoms: 4–5x latency on user-facing generate calls, elevated 5xx error rate (peaked ~6.8%), and throughput throttling that caused order-confirmation stalls. This directly affected a subset of checkout flows.

We need: an exec-level summary, ETA for full remediation, and confirmation of credits/SLAs for impact. Our procurement and platform teams are on standby and require clear next steps.

I’ve attached the logs we pulled from our edge (initial-incident-logs.zip). Please escalate.

—Jordan
VP, Platform Engineering
Zenith Retail
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@zenithretail.com>

Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Urgent: production instability during flash sale

Jordan — thanks for the heads-up and for sending the logs. I’m escalating to our on-call ops and platform leads (cc’d) and we’ll treat this as a Sev-1 until verified otherwise. Immediate plan:

- Short-term mitigation (now): route affected tenant traffic to the dedicated fallback pool; enable prefetched KV caches for common prefixes.
- In parallel: ops will collect full token-level telemetry and a narrowed set of traces to identify whether latency is kernel/quantization/IO bound.
- We’ll deliver: (a) an exec summary for you by COB Mon 11/30, (b) a full RCA + action tracker by EOD Tue 12/01.

Can the Zenith team share any unusual query patterns or model pins for the window? That will help. I’ll coordinate a 30-min exec readout for stakeholder alignment — proposed Mon 12/1 16:00 ET; let me know if that works.

—Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.ai, rachel.kim@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@zenithretail.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production instability during flash sale

Quick technical read: we’ve pulled the token-level traces and a few things stand out — transient KV cache thrashing when sequence lengths spiked (bulk report-generation calls), combined with a degraded kernel path on the older quantized variant (Q4-8) under sustained 12–14k token windows. That created backpressure in the batching layer and raised tail latency.

Immediate remedial actions (I’m owning the kernel side):
- 11/28 12:00 ET: force-roll traffic away from Q4-8 to Q4-16 variant for Zenith for the next 48 hours (in progress).
- 11/28–11/30: deploy micro patch to improve KV eviction heuristics and reduce cache thrash (canary 11/29, full rollout 11/30).
- 11/30 18:00 ET: validate throughput and tail-p99 latency; if not within target, enable temporary autoscale headroom for Zenith.

I’ve attached a short CSV with sample throughput windows (throughput-samples.csv). Will provide the RCA write-up by Mon EOD.

—Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Serving Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@zenithretail.com>, procurement@zenithretail.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -05:00
Subject: RCA & action tracker — Zenith Retail incident (Nov 27)

Team / Jordan — attaching the formal RCA (RCA-Zenith-20261130.pdf) and the action tracker (action-tracker-zenith-2026.csv). Executive summary below; full details are in the attachment.

Executive summary:
- Root cause: interaction between large sequence-length workloads (reporting job spikes from Zenith) and an eviction regression in Q4-8 quantized kernel that caused sustained KV cache thrash and batching backpressure.
- Impact window: 2026-11-27T18:32–2026-11-27T21:07 ET. Peak 5xx ~6.8%; tail-p99 latency increased ~4–5x.
- Immediate remediations completed: forced traffic off Q4-8, canary of KV patch, temporary autoscale headroom applied.
- Customer-facing actions: committed to a credit of two days of reserved capacity billing; scheduled a technical runbook review with Zenith PS.

Action tracker (high-level):
- Vivek kulkarni — kernel eviction patch, canary complete 11/29, full rollout 11/30, verify metrics by 11/30 18:00 ET.
- Evelyn hart — update monitoring dashboards and add RTT/eviction counters; enable alerting thresholds for cache-thrash patterns by 12/03.
- Dylan brooks — QoS policy change to prioritize checkout traffic during scheduled sales windows; policy draft by 12/04.
- Rachel kim — customer comms, credit paperwork, schedule runbook workshop; draft to customer by 12/01.
- Alex martinez — exec readout and weekly closure summary until all actions complete.

Next steps: we’ll run a joint validation on 12/03 during a synthetic load window; Evelyn will confirm pass/fail and mark items complete. Jordan — please confirm if the proposed credit and 12/01 workshop are acceptable.

Attachments: RCA-Zenith-20261130.pdf, action-tracker-zenith-2026.csv

Quick verification update: the canary rollout looks good. Post-rollout aggregated metrics in the 11/30 16:00–23:00 ET window show p99 latency back to baseline for Zenith and error rate down to ~0.8% during controlled load. I ran synthetic load at the requested profile and did not reproduce the tail behavior.

I’ll be completing the monitoring additions by 12/03 and will open follow-up tickets to add eviction counters to our long-term dashboards. Marking the kernel patch validation as PASSED for now; will update the action-tracker-zenith-2026.csv with timestamps.

Subject: Closure note & ask for exec signoff on credit — Zenith Retail incident

Team / Execs — quick closure summary for your awareness and a small ask for signoff. This thread documents the Zenith Retail outage window (11/27) and the follow-through. Key points:
- Impact: transient but customer-visible latency and 5xxs during a high-load window; Zenith experienced checkout delays.
- Technical mitigation: kernel eviction patch rolled 11/30, canary validated, monitoring additions in progress.
- Business remediation: CS has proposed a goodwill credit (2 days reserved capacity); procurement has acknowledged receipt and is reviewing.
- Current status: all high-priority actions are in verified or in-progress state; target full closure 12/06 after post-validation load test on 12/03.

Ask: please reply to this thread with APPROVE or QUESTIONS on the proposed credit. If no objections by EOD Fri 12/03 PT we’ll proceed with the credit and mark the account remediated in our tracking system.

Thanks — I’ll continue weekly summaries until the tracker is 100% closed.

—Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
